draft.title: Power in popular culture
card: Power in popular culture is the ability to shape what is made, promoted and noticed. A few large media companies hold much of this power.
They can pay for production, advertising and distribution. This helps them decide which films, songs and shows reach large audiences.
It lets ordinary people make and share their own content, often without a large company. Some users build large audiences this way.
So power is not held by one group only. Large companies still hold much of it, and social media gives ordinary people a way to take part.
draft.remember: Large companies hold much of the power, but social media lets ordinary people share it.

a.q: Which statement best describes who holds power in popular culture?
opts: Companies hold much of it, and social media users share some
Companies hold all of it, and social media users hold none
Social media users hold all of it, and companies hold none
Power is split evenly between companies and social media users
a.why: The card says a few large companies hold much of the power, while social media lets ordinary people create and spread culture too. The option that gives companies all the power is tempting, but it ignores what social media users can do.
a.clue: Look for the option where both groups hold some power.

b.q: Priya films short comedy clips in her kitchen in Geelong and posts them online. Thousands of people now watch them. What does this best show?
opts: Ordinary people can create and spread popular culture
Large media companies no longer have any power
Popular culture is always made by ordinary people
Online clips are only popular if a company promotes them
b.why: Priya made and shared her content without a large company, which shows social media gives ordinary people a way to shape popular culture. It does not show companies have lost all power, because they can still control much of what is produced and promoted.
b.clue: One success does not remove the power of large companies.

a.q: Why do a few large media companies hold much of the power in popular culture?
opts: They can fund production, advertising and distribution
They copy the trends that ordinary users start online
They stop ordinary people posting content on social media
They let audiences vote on which shows get made
a.why: Paying for production, advertising and distribution lets large companies decide what reaches big audiences. Copying trends from users is tempting, but it would show users leading, not companies holding power.
a.clue: Think about what it takes to reach a large audience.

b.q: Priya films comedy clips in her kitchen in Geelong and posts them online with no company behind her. Thousands now watch. What does this best show?
opts: Social media lets ordinary people spread popular culture
Large media companies have lost their power to promote
Priya's success comes from a media company's advertising
Popular culture now comes mainly from ordinary people
b.why: Priya made and shared her clips without a company, which shows social media lets ordinary people take part in shaping popular culture. It does not show companies have lost their power, because they still control much of what is produced and promoted.
b.clue: Does one creator's success change who holds most of the power?
